items.summary: The Marine Corps on Monday held a ceremony to mark the 16th anniversary of South Korea's victory in an artillery attack in 2010 by North Korea on a border island that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The ceremony was held at Daejeon National Cemetery in Daejeon, some 140 kilometers south of Seoul, on the occasion of the 16th anniversary of the North's artillery attack on Yeonpyeong Island on Nov. 23, 2010. North Korea's shelling of the island marked its first attack on a civilian area in the South since the 1950-53 Korean War. During Monday's event, Vice Defense Minister Lee Doo-hee said the South Korean military will maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure its victory against any enemy threats. "Our military will immediately respond to any enemy threat or provocation and maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure absolute victory," Lee said in his commemorative address. "To achieve this, we will push to restructure the military system so that the Marine Corps will be enhanced to a quasi-fourth service," he added. Three officials from the NEC headquarters appeared at the Seoul Central District Court in the morning, refusing to answer reporters' questions before entering the courtroom. Hearings for the remaining five officials from regional NEC offices were set to be held later in the afternoon. The court was expected to decide whether to issue the warrants later in the day at the earliest. Requests for the warrants were filed Wednesday by special counsel Lee Tae-han's team on suspicions that the election officials entered false voter turnout figures while voting was under way or forged vote count sheets during the race for the education superintendent of Gyeonggi Province, with some of them allegedly involved in multiple cases. items.summary: Ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) Chairman Kim Min-seok heads into his 100th day in office on Tuesday, as party support slips amid a deepening factional feud, in stark contrast to the turnaround he promised. Kim pledged during his leadership campaign to raise the DPK’s support by at least 10 percentage points within three months. But a Gallup Korea poll released on Friday put the DPK’s support at 36 percent, down from 41 percent in a survey conducted from Aug. 11–13, just before Kim took office on Aug. 17. Under the circumstances, Kim’s leadership will face another test as he tries to reunite the DPK and win over centrist voters while the party’s hard-liners push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae — a move that could rally its base and alienate moderates. “It appears the voters still don’t feel they can count on the ruling party to settle problems under Kim’s leadership,” said Jung Jae-hwan, a political science professor at Inha University. “The move to impeach the chief justice will test whether Kim can keep the party focused on voters’ everyd

items.summary: The education ministry was set to file criminal complaints Monday against five people caught cheating with smart devices during last week's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), a senior ministry official said. The ministry previously announced that 111 suspected cases of cheating involving electronic devices were detected during the annual college entrance exam held Thursday amid growing public concerns over the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to cheat on national exams. Of those cases, five involved the actual use of devices such as smart glasses and miniature cameras, according to the ministry. Complaints have already been filed against some of the five test-takers, and the process for all five will be completed before the day's end, Shin Jin-yong, head of the ministry's University Admissions Policy Division, said in a media briefing. items.summary: A family member of the late top scorer of this year's law school entrance exam appeared before police Monday as investigators step up a probe into allegations that he cheated on the test. The late Lee Jin-woo, a 32-year-old dental student, was found dead Thursday after facing suspicions of cheating by using artificial intelligence (AI) to earn a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET). Despite his death, police have pressed ahead with the investigation on suspicion of fraud and other charges, after a group of lawyers earlier filed a police complaint. Earlier in the day, a family member of Lee appeared before the financial crime unit under the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. Police were expected to ask Lee's family member for cooperation in turning over evidence, such as his mobile phone. Lee's academic achievements came under widespread scrutiny following the recent admission by the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam that he had cheated with the help of AI. items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung nominated Lim Woong-soon, his second deputy national security adviser and a former ambassador to Canada, as foreign minister, Monday, in a Cabinet reshuffle. Lim would succeed Cho Hyun. Lee also nominated Hong Ihk-pyo, a former presidential secretary for political affairs and former floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), as unification minister. Former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil was nominated to head the National Intelligence Service. The president also nominated Rep. Han Jun-ho of the DPK as interior minister and presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung as culture minister. Presidential chief of Staff Lim Kwang-hyun announced the nominations during a briefing at Cheng Wa Dae.

items.title: Jongno District deploys AI crosswalks to give slower pedestrians more time

items.summary: Jongno District in central Seoul is upgrading its intersections with artificial intelligence (AI), pavement-level LED lights and automated voice alerts to help pedestrians — especially children and older adults — cross streets more safely. The district office said it will begin operating pavement-mounted pedestrian signals and voice guidance devices at 123 locations from Dec. 1 with an AI-powered system that automatically extends crossing time. The pavement-level pedestrian signals illuminate the tactile pavers, a kind of ground surface indicator to assist disabled pedestrians, at crosswalks to help people detect when it is safe to cross. Voice guidance devices use infrared sensors to detect pedestrians and issue audible warnings when they attempt to cross against the signal, as well as announcing when the light turns green. The installations target roads with at least four lanes, prioritizing areas with heavy pedestrian traffic and a history of accidents. items.title: US Forces Korea deploys Apache, Blackhawk helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan
items.title_zh: 驻韩美军在日本部署阿帕奇、黑鹰直升机进行实弹演习
items.summary: The U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) recently deployed its helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan, the first time such assets have been sent outside the Korean Peninsula for exercises, the USFK said Monday. The 2nd Infantry Division's 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade deployed the AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, the UH-60 Black Hawk multirole utility helicopters and the CH-47 Chinook transport helicopters to the Combined Arms Training Center (CATC) at Camp Fuji, located in Shizuoka Prefecture, the USFK said in a social media post. It said the "historic first" deployment of the choppers was aimed at strengthening its readiness in the Indo-Pacific. The AH-64 Apache serves as a heavily armed attack helicopter designed to hunt and destroy enemy tanks and armored vehicles with missiles and rockets, while the UH-60 Black Hawk is a core asset primarily tasked with airlifting troops into combat zones, transporting supplies and evacuating wounded soldiers. The CH-47 Chinook is a heavy-lift transport helicopter used to move large numbers of troops, heavy artillery and bulk supplies across the battlefield.

The PPP's move came after the DPK-controlled National Assembly railroaded the bill earlier this month that mandates a special counsel investigation into suspicions that prosecutors under the previous administration had indicted President Lee Jae Myung and others on fabricated evidence. PPP lawmakers had boycotted the vote in protest. The PPP claimed that its lawmakers were not given sufficient time to review and deliberate on the details of the bill before its passage and said it filed a competence dispute against National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik and DPK Rep. Seo Young-kyo, chair of the parliamentary legislation and judiciary committee. items.summary: Seoul is expanding its ambitions in biotechnology, transforming its food startup center into a platform designed to connect promising agricultural and food technology companies with major corporations, investors and global distribution networks. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday it had relaunched the Seoul Food Startup Center as the Seoul Green Bio Hub, broadening its focus from food manufacturing and distribution to technology-driven businesses built around agricultural and biological resources. Green biotechnology applies biological technologies to agricultural and other biological resources to create new products and commercial opportunities in sectors including food and agriculture. Of the 884 green bio companies registered nationwide with the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, 89 are based in Seoul, according to the city. The new hub will expand partnerships between startups and major corporations through open innovation programs, matching companies' technologies and ideas with corporate business needs and distribution networks. items.title: Saudi Arabia strongly condemns drone attacks targeting Khartoum
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯强烈谴责针对喀土穆的无人机袭击
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed Saudi Arabia’s strong condemnation of the drone attacks targeting the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, including the attack on a United Nations building, which resulted in civilian casualties and damage to civilian infrastructure and facilities. In a statement, the ministry said: “The Kingdom categorically rejects these brutal attacks and stresses the importance of respecting international humanitarian law, fulfilling the obligation to protect civilians, civilian facilities, and the premises of international organizations, ensuring the safety of their personnel, and sparing the Sudanese people further suffering.” Saudi Arabia reiterated its steadfast position calling for the preservation of Sudan’s security, stability, unity, sovereignty, and legitimate institutions. The ministry also extended the Kingdom’s sincere condolences to the families of the victims and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

items.title: Interior minister lays foundation stone for Unified Security Operations Center in Hail
items.title_zh: 内政大臣为哈伊勒统一安全运营中心奠基
items.summary: HAIL — Minister of Interior Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud bin Naif laid the foundation stone for the Unified Security Operations Center (911) in the Hail region on Sunday. The ceremony was held in the presence of Emir of Hail Prince Abdulaziz bin Saad. The minister was briefed on the project, which is one of the Ministry of Interior’s strategic initiatives. Being implemented in cooperation with the Quality of Life Program, one of the Saudi Vision 2030 programs, the project aims to unify emergency numbers and operations centers across the Kingdom’s regions. This will strengthen integration among security and service agencies and enhance operational response efficiency. Prince Abdulaziz also viewed a presentation introducing the center, outlining the functions of its operations rooms and the mechanisms governing their work within an integrated operational system. The center comprises four operations rooms at the regional level and will serve the city of Hail and eight governorates, thereby enhancing emergency response efficiency. Deputy Emir of Hail Prince Faisal bin Fahd and a number of senior officials attended the foundation-stone laying ceremony. **media[2798361]** During the visit, the minister of interior met with members of the security committee in the Hail region, in the presence of the Emir of Hail. The minister was briefed on the security committee’s work and responsibilities, particularly its role in coordinating the efforts of security and military agencies and monitoring all matters relating to the region’s security. Prince Abdulaziz commended the dedicated efforts of security and military personnel in carrying out their duties, praising their devotion and loyalty in safeguarding security and serving their religion, their King and their country. He directed the committee members to convey his greetings and appreciation to personnel across their respective sectors.

items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯的数字化转型率超过 90%，每年可节省 260 亿沙特里亚尔
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Digital Government Authority Governor Eng. Ahmed Alsuwaiyan highlighted the major achievements of the Kingdom’s digital transformation, noting that the digital transformation rate is expected to exceed 90 percent by the end of 2026. These achievements have generated annual savings of more than SR26 billion and eliminated over 1.3 million daily in-person visits through the delivery of digital services, he said. Speaking at the government press conference organized by the Ministry of Media, Alsuwaiyan explained that the Ministry of Interior’s services through the “Absher” platform have helped expedite transactions, streamline procedures, and enhance the user experience. Many services that previously took four hours to complete can now be delivered in just 30 seconds.He noted that 95 percent of court sessions are now conducted remotely through virtual courts, significantly reducing the duration of judicial proceedings from 219 days to just 20 days and eliminating more than 60 million annual visits to judicial facilities. In the Hajj and Umrah sector, the number of users of the Nusk platform has surpassed 60 million, while Al-Rawdah Al-Sharifah at the Prophet’s Mosque accommodates 55,000 visitors daily. Procedures for issuing Hajj and Umrah visas have also been streamlined, with the process now taking just five minutes, compared to five days previously, while more than 22 million visas are expected to be issued by 2025.In the healthcare sector, 51 percent of medical appointments are now provided remotely, while medication dispensing time has been cut to less than eight minutes, compared to 72 hours previously. These improvements have generated savings of SR1.5 billion in medication costs.Alsuwaiyan said that Saudi Arabia has also made more than 1,800 government services accessible through the Tawakkalna application, processing over 88 million transactions daily. Electronic payments now account for 85 percent of all financial transactions, while customs clearance time has been reduced to just two hours. Similarly, the time required to purchase and supply goods and services has been shortened to two days.As part of efforts to harness artificial intelligence to enhance productivity and operational efficiency, the Ministry of Energy has successfully reduced the time required to process and monitor oil and gas supplies to just 30 seconds, compared to 25 minutes previously.Meanwhile, total donations through the Ihsan platform have reached SR17 billion through more than 390,000 donation transactions. The service for requesting domestic worker recruitment has also been streamlined, with the process now taking only eight minutes and eliminating the need for in-person visits to social insurance offices.Alsuwaiyan underscored the importance of national regulations and technical standards in advancing digital services and enhancing government performance. He noted that the digital transformation measurement index had climbed from 69 percent in 2021 to more than 90 percent by the end of 2026. He further revealed that the cost of monitoring visual pollution had declined by 76 percent while groundwater sustainability services had generated financial savings of SR120 million.He added that these achievements had propelled the Kingdom’s ranking in the overall E-Government Development Index from 52nd place in 2018 to fourth place in 2026 among 194 countries, bringing it closer to achieving the Saudi Vision 2030 target of becoming one of the world’s top five governments in e-governance sector.

items.title: Crown Prince, Bulgarian PM discuss expanding bilateral cooperation in Riyadh
items.title_zh: 沙特王储与保加利亚总理在利雅得讨论扩大双边合作
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman received Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev in Riyadh on Sunday.During their official meeting, the Crown Prince and Radev reviewed the longstanding bilateral relations between the two countries, explored avenues for expanding cooperation, and discussed promising opportunities to further strengthen their partnership across various sectors. They also exchanged views on the latest regional and international developments and the ongoing efforts to address them. **media[2798091]** An official welcoming ceremony was held and it was followed by their official meeting. At the outset of the meeting, the Crown Prince welcomed the prime minister of Bulgaria to Saudi Arabia. On his part, Radev expressed his pleasure at the visit and the opportunity to meet with the Crown Prince. Those who attended the reception included Deputy Emir of Riyadh Prince Mohammed bin Abdulrahman; Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan; Minister of State, Member of the Cabinet and National Security Advisor Dr. Musaed Al-Aiban; Minister of Commerce Dr. Majid Al-Qasabi, (the accompanying minister); Minister of Tourism Ahmed Al-Khateeb; Minister of Communications and Information Technology Eng. Abdullah Alswaha; Minister of Economy and Planning Faisal Al-Ibrahim; and Saudi Ambassador to Bulgaria Dr. Rami Al-Otaibi. From the Bulgarian side, the reception was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy, Investments, and Industry Alexander Pulev; Minister of the Interior Ivan Demerdzhiev; Minister of Transport and Communications Georgi Peev; Minister of Innovation and Digital Transformation Ivan Vassilev; Minister of Tourism Ilin Dimitrov; and Bulgarian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Lyubomir Nikolov Popov.

items.title: KFSH performs nearly two-thirds of liver transplants in Saudi Arabia
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯近三分之二的肝脏移植手术由KFSH完成
items.summary: RIYADH — King Faisal Specialist Hospital & Research Centre (KFSH) performed approximately 63% of all liver transplants in Saudi Arabia in 2023 and 2024 combined, accounting for nearly two-thirds of the 1,018 procedures recorded by the Saudi Center for Organ Transplantation (SCOT).The hospital also performed nearly half of all kidney transplants conducted across the Kingdom during the same period.KFSH has performed more than 1,000 solid organ transplants annually for four consecutive years, with a total of 4,330 procedures between 2022 and 2025, including 1,109 in 2025 alone.The procedures included kidney, liver, heart, lung, pancreas and intestine transplants.The hospital's kidney transplant program reported one-year patient and graft survival rates ranging from 97% to 99%.KFSH's transplant clinics also recorded approximately 86,000 follow-up visits in 2025 as part of an integrated care system aimed at preserving patients' health and maintaining the long-term function of transplanted organs.The hospital continues to advance surgical techniques in organ transplantation, having performed the world's first fully robotic liver transplant in 2023, followed by the world's first fully robotic heart transplant in 2024.These medical milestones have helped reduce surgical trauma associated with complex transplant procedures.KFSH ranked first in the Middle East and Africa and 12th globally among the world's top 250 academic medical centers for 2026.It was also named the most valuable healthcare brand in Saudi Arabia and the Middle East for 2026 by Brand Finance.The hospital has also been featured in Newsweek's World's Best Hospitals 2026, World's Best Smart Hospitals 2027 and World's Best Specialized Hospitals 2027 rankings.

items.title: Saudi Customs ports record 1,053 contraband seizures last week
items.title_zh: 沙特海关港口上周查获1053起走私案件
items.summary: RIYADH — Land, sea, and air Customs ports across Saudi Arabia recorded 1,053 seizures of prohibited goods last week. The seizures included 31 types of narcotics, such as hashish, cocaine, heroin, and Captagon pills; 263 other prohibited substances; and 781 cases involving tobacco. This was part of the efforts of the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) to combat smuggling and protect society. ZATCA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening customs oversight of the Kingdom’s imports and exports in coordination with relevant authorities. The authority urged the public to help combat smuggling and protect the national economy by reporting suspicious activities through its security hotline (1910), email (1910@zatca.gov.sa), or international number (009661910). All reports concerning smuggling and violations of the Unified Customs Law are treated as strictly confidential. Financial rewards are also offered for information proven accurate, it said.

items.title: Saudi Arabia, Bulgaria to strengthen AI, technology partnership
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯与保加利亚将加强人工智能和技术合作
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Communications and Information Technology Abdullah Alswaha met with Bulgarian Minister of Innovation and Digital Transformation Ivan Vasilev in Riyadh on Sunday. During the meeting, they discussed prospects for partnership between the two countries in artificial intelligence, technology innovation, and capacity development, in support of digital economy growth. The ministers reviewed opportunities to strengthen cooperation in developing innovative solutions, exchanging expertise in building digital capabilities, supporting technology entrepreneurship, and expanding partnerships between companies in the two countries.

items.title: Saudi Arabia's date production rises 7.6% to over 2 million tons in 2025
items.title_zh: 2025年沙特阿拉伯的枣产量将增长7.6%，超过200万吨
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia's date production rose 7.6 percent year-on-year to over 2 million tons in 2025, while the number of palm trees reached 37.9 million, including 34.7 million fruit-bearing trees. The General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT) revealed in its Agricultural Statistics 2025 report that the Khalas variety led date production at 654,800 tons, with 11.1 million palm trees, including 10.2 million fruit-bearing trees. Meanwhile, total grain production reached approximately 1.5 million tons, with wheat accounting for 65.8 percent, or 965,700 tons, down 18.6 percent compared with 2024. Open-field vegetable production rose 5.5 percent to approximately 2.9 million tons, led by potatoes at 653,000 tons and watermelons at 633,000 tons. Greenhouse vegetable production also increased by 3.8 percent to approximately 828,000 tons, with tomatoes accounting for 343,400 tons and cucumbers 240,900 tons. The report also showed that the number of permanent trees, excluding date palms, reached 44.8 million, with production exceeding 1 million tons, up 4.7 percent year-on-year. Olive trees accounted for the largest share, with 22.1 million trees and production totaling 361,000 tons. Meanwhile, organic farming and areas under conversion produced 87,000 tons, marking an 11.5 percent decline compared with 2024.Agricultural exports rose 21.5 percent to 614,000 tons, while agricultural crop imports increased 7.7 percent to 20.2 million tons. The report draws on the 2025 Agricultural Survey and administrative records from the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, the Agricultural Development Fund and the Saudi Central Bank.
